ledger_updates.evidence: Proof 1.2 uses |x-hG_i x+O(h^2)|<=2|x| to transfer Schwartz decay to an evaluated derivative. An upper bound does not prove that decay; exact orthogonality gives |R_i(-t)x|=|x|. Integrating the orbit derivative gives a bound C_N|x|(1+|x|)^(-N), whose square is integrable for sufficiently large N, proving the stated L2 derivative. F6 also cites CCR clause (a), but the identity is clause (b).

ledger_updates.evidence: Proof 2.1 says coordinate multiplication is bounded exactly where x_j is. Both coordinate operators are unbounded; domain preservation is the substitution identity integral |x_j f(-x)|^2 dx = integral |x_j f(x)|^2 dx, so the required L2 products exist together.
ledger_updates.minimality: Replace only the parenthetical justification by the exact domain-integrability equality; no Statement change is necessary.
